key_insight: A fault-tolerant, literature-grounded LLM pipeline can autonomously go from corpus mining to a publication-ready computational physics manuscript while avoiding hallucinated science through repeated external calibration.
engineering_relevance: The work suggests a practical architecture for high-stakes scientific agents: fresh-context isolation, on-disk shared state, reproduction-based checkpoints, and adversarial review to enforce verifiable progress.
method: Mapped 11,083 recent condensed-matter arXiv papers to identify a research direction.
Ran 47 fresh-context sessions across six phases with only shared on-disk state and 2,162 literature-consultation events.
Used reproducibility checkpoints and bounded human intervention only when reference reproduction failed.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an end-to-end demonstration on altermagnetic piezomagnetism with three substantive physics findings, plus ablation comparisons that isolate calibration as the key grounding mechanism.
watch_item: The pipeline’s reliability depends on accessible reference literature and reproduction-friendly toolchains, so its performance may drop in less documented or less benchmarkable domains.
paper_title: Grounded autonomous research: a fault-tolerant LLM pipeline from corpus to manuscript in frontier computational physics
